newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Kosovo Albanian dies in prison.
newsitem.headline: Kosovo Albanian dies in prison.

text.p: An ethnic Albanian arrested on suspicion of terrorist activities in the Serbian province of Kosovo hanged himself in police custody, Monday media reports quoted Kosovo police as saying.

But the leading ethnic Albanian party, the Demcratic League of Kosovo (LDK), said in a statement that the man, Besnik Restelica, had "died a violent death, arguably of tortures at the hands of the Serb security".
It said Restelica's lawyer Fazli Balaj was denied permission to see his client for several days before his death on Saturday.

Restelica was arrested in January as a suspected member of the Liberation Army of Kosovo, an obscure organisation which has taken responsibility for most of a handful of killings of Serb policemen and other Serbs over the past year.

Serb police killed three ethnic Albanians in a gunbattle in Kosovo's main city, Pristina, in late January. Dozens were arrested and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic congratulated Serb interior ministry officials for what he termed an "anti-terrorist operation".
The LDK statement said: "Restelica is the sixth Albanian to have died of Serb police hand so far this year."
Police are reported as saying that Restelica hanged himself in his cell using two T-shirts tied to a bed.

In 1989, Milosevic abolished the autonomous status of impoverished Kosovo, where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one, on the grounds that its Albanians were preparing to secede from Serbia. Nationalist Serbs say Kosovo is the ancient cradle of their culture.
The province has been widely seen as a powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
